newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Canada's First Quantum to develop Zambia mine.
newsitem.headline: Canada's First Quantum to develop Zambia mine.

text.p: First Quantum Minerals Ltd will develop Zambia's Bwana Mkubwa copper mine and aims to produce 10,000 tonnes of copper a year, financiers Investec Bank Ltd said on Tuesday.
The mine at Ndola in the Copperbelt province was closed in 1984 when owners Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM) allowed the mining licence to lapse.
Investec said the Bwanga Mkuba mine licence was the first to be issued under Zambia's new mining and minerals act.

"This project, which is to become one of the first privately operated mines on the Copperbelt, is to be developed utilising project finance and technical expertise from South Africa," Investec said in a statement.
The project involved the construction of a $25 million plant to recover copper from tailings deposited by previous operations.
Initial production was estimated at 10,000 tonnes of copper a year for a five-year period. This would generate income of around $100 million, Investec said.
Investec said it had played a major role in financing recent central African mining projects.

"Amongst Investec's more notable transactions are a $15 million loan to ZCCM for the construction of a tailings flotation plant, a $41.2 million loan to Gecamines in Zaire for various rehabilitation projects and a $9.8 million loan to Maamba Collieries in Zambia for rehabilitation work," Investec said.
Zambia is in the throes of a privatisation drive, which would see the mining and power assets of ZCCM -- the largest public enterprise in the country -- sold.
